- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, missing the true price’s gradual mean reversion or late-stage stabilization.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 68.27 → 75.19) are common, suggesting model fails to account for market correction after volatility.
- Model underestimates late-stage price trends (last 5–10 days of 30d), particularly when true prices rise steadily toward 75+.
- Forecast bias is stronger for higher price ranges (>70) — model tends to overpredict in upward momentum phases.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing true price direction — often misreads trend continuation or reversal.
- Mean reversion is under-estimated: model holds high forecasts too long, failing to adjust downward when price shows signs of cooling.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggesting model lacks adaptive horizon calibration.
